doc.title: Ametria Dock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 4, 2019

title: Advice for her 13-year-old daughter Kayla about music and school
summary: Kayla won a school talent show and wants to do production and engineering; Dock and her husband encourage school for technique and theory, though TV opportunities exist.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You have a daughter who’s what, a teenager?
Afterwards on the drive home last night I was thinking about when I was deciding about a career in music that my parents really didn’t have any advice except get that teaching degree.
You have a bit more relevant advice for your daughter. What would you tell her about the music business at this point?

So actually we’ve been talking about it. So my daughter is a straight A student. She is doing so well. And it’s funny, she just did a talent show and won the all-school talent show this year, a couple of days ago. And I sat there and my mom and dad and my in- laws and our whole family was there to support her. And my mom was sitting and crying so hard. And she just looked over and she said, “This just reminds me of you all over again. I see what’s happening.” And she said, “But I see something different with Kayla.” So my daughter is really — she loves science and she loves music. I mean her passion for music, I see myself in her. But she wants to create more — she wants to do more of the production, musical production. She wants to write music, she wants to create the music, she wants to engineer. So I see her going down a different path but I see her doing actually more than what I’ve done at this point. I see that happening. But I see her definitely going to school. I think, and I say this, I learned everything by ear, I got my start so young, and I wish I had — I did have community and accountability, but in a different way apart from school. So I had people that were doing this and doing well but see I want her to still be able to go to school and do this music and learn the technique and the theory. I think that that would be helpful for where she wants to go, what I see happening for her. So my husband and myself are both encouraging for her to go to school, because I know that she can go deeper within what it is that she is talking about now with us. And we’re having really, really in-depth conversations about it now. But she’s also got opportunities right now to do television. So we’re in that.
Which is wonderful and it also makes things a little harder.
